groups.body:
Surface: infra

**Related:** #3429, #3507, #3509, #3563, #3564, #3565, #3581

## Current State

The post-merge `windows-regression` workflow (run 39212936982, on `windows-latest`) flagged `tests/pipeline-run-dir-adoption-anchoring.test.js` as newly failing after PR #3547 merged as `a865bb71d` (#2870's change). The excerpt names one test, but the file's full Windows log shows **all five tests failing**, and the latest run (39242652806, HEAD `7eaa543fc`, base `df15212d5`) still fails all five. That run lists the file under `baselineFailing`, so it is now a failure inherited at base. The file's tests, test names abbreviated:

| # | Test (line on `origin/main`) | Windows error |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | adoption anchoring (shared snippet): trapped `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` rejected (85) | `skills/_shared/run-dir-resolution.md must have a "## Bash snippet (resolution)" fenced bash block — extraction pattern is out of sync with the doc` |
| 2 | adoption anchoring (shared snippet): anchored value still adopted (115) | same |
| 3 | adoption anchoring (wrap-up's own copy): trapped value rejected (85) | `skills/wrap-up/SKILL.md must have a "### Establish the run directory (unconditional)" section with a fenced bash block — extraction pattern is out of sync with the doc` |
| 4 | adoption anchoring (wrap-up's own copy): anchored value still adopted (115) | same |
| 5 | step 2 (shared snippet): a non-canonical dir is never adopted over a canonical match (138) | the shared-snippet message again |

Why the record says "newly": `a865bb71d` added test 5. Tests 1-4 were already failing on Windows for the same reason, and the new test 5 gave the file a new failing test identity.

Root cause, test-side only. The suite reads both skill files with a raw `fs.readFileSync(…, 'utf8')` (lines 24-31). Its extractors anchor on bare `\n`: `/## Bash snippet \(resolution\)\n\n```bash\n([\s\S]*?)\n```/` (line 35) and `/### Establish the run directory \(unconditional\)[\s\S]*?```bash\n([\s\S]*?)\n```/` (line 49). A Windows checkout with `core.autocrlf=true` gives both files `\r\n` line endings, because `.gitattributes` pins only `tools/upstream-drift/fixtures/**`. Neither regex then matches, and every test fails at the extractor's `assert.ok`. The skill prose is correct.

Reproduced in scratch on macOS against `origin/main` copies of the test and both skill files, with the two docs rewritten to CRLF (`perl -pi -e 's/\r?\n/\r\n/'`). This is a CRLF simulation, not a Windows run:

- Unchanged test against the CRLF docs: `# pass 0` / `# fail 5`, with exactly the two extractor messages above. This matches the Windows log test for test.
- Regex-only fix (`\r?\n` in both patterns): still `# fail 5`, now with `bash: -c: line 8: syntax error near unexpected token $'in\r'` and `unexpected end of file from 'if' command`. The captured snippet keeps its `\r`s, and bash cannot run it.
- Reading both files through `tests/helpers/read-skill.js`'s `readText()`: `# pass 5` / `# fail 0` on the CRLF docs and on the LF docs.

A second Windows-only failure is expected behind the CRLF one in test 5. It is inferred, not observed, because the extractor fails first on Windows today. Test 5 asserts `strictEqual(resolved, canonical)`. In the shared snippet, `resolved` comes from `find "$RUN_ROOT/…"`, and `RUN_ROOT` comes from `cd … && pwd`. Under Git Bash, `pwd` prints the MSYS form `/d/a/_temp/…`, while `canonical` is the native `D:\a\_temp\…` path built by `path.join`. So the full-string compare cannot match on Windows even when the snippet picks the right directory. Tests 1-4 should not hit this:

- Test 1 (shared snippet) resolves to `''`, which skips the `startsWith` check.
- Test 2 (shared snippet) returns the raw native env value unchanged.
- Tests 3-4 (wrap-up) get their path from `node bin/hooks.js resolve-run-dir`. That command's native-path equality pins in `tests/hooks-run-dir-resolve.test.js` pass on `windows-latest`.

The `windows-checkout-test-parity` skill's Anti-Patterns row "Treating a CRLF fix as the whole Windows fix for a test that extracts and runs a skill's shell snippet" records the same two-layer shape from #3517.

Repo-wide sibling grep on `origin/main` (`1c8cda70b`): `git grep -lE '```(bash|sh|js|json|yaml|yml)?\\n' -- tests tools`, cross-checked by hand against each file's read and against the latest Windows run's failing set. 14 other files apply a bare-`\n` fence regex (or a `'\n```\n'` search) to a raw read of live markdown, and all 14 fail on `windows-latest` with an extractor-not-found message:

- Already claimed by an open record:
  - `tests/specify-ceremony-tally-prose.test.js` and `tests/specify-crossref-manifest-resolve.test.js` (#3587)
  - `tests/console-autoresolve-drain-overlap-carveout.test.js` (#3565)
  - `tests/skill-load-report-cli.test.js` (#3574)
- Claimed by no open record (an issue search for each filename returns nothing):
  - `tests/bin-lib/issues/labels.test.js`
  - `tests/blast-radius-snippet.test.js`
  - `tests/capture-native-branch-guard-shapes.test.js`
  - `tests/harness-health-runaway-section.test.js`
  - `tests/init-port-isolation-conformance.test.js`
  - `tests/plan-audit-check-e-prose.test.js`
  - `tests/tidy-release-note-repair-conformance.test.js`
  - `tests/dispatch-firing-exclusion.test.js`
  - `tests/multispec-not-run-callsite.test.js`
  - `tests/verify-expectations-writer-conformance.test.js`

The other grep hits are out of scope. `tests/bin-lib/harness-health/issue-payload.test.js`, `tests/comment-trust-conformance.test.js` and `tests/payload-boundary.test.js` match only on in-test string literals. The files that already read through `readText()` (for example `tests/adopted-branch-collision-snippet-fixture.test.js`) pass on Windows.

## Deliverables

1. `tests/pipeline-run-dir-adoption-anchoring.test.js`: read `plugin/skills/_shared/run-dir-resolution.md` and `plugin/skills/wrap-up/SKILL.md` through `tests/helpers/read-skill.js`'s `readText()` instead of raw `fs.readFileSync`. The extracted snippets are then LF on every checkout, which is what makes them runnable by `bash -c`. Leave both extraction regexes as they are.
2. Same file, test 5 (line 147): replace `assert.strictEqual(resolved, canonical)` with a comparison by directory name, `assert.strictEqual(path.basename(resolved), path.basename(canonical))`. Add a one-line comment saying the shared snippet's step-2 path comes from `pwd` and is MSYS-form under Git Bash. `tests/hooks-run-dir-resolve.test.js` lines 186 and 210 already pin step-2 picks by `path.basename`. The test still separates the canonical pick (`2026-09-20T080000-…`) from the stale one (`20260911T131119-…`).
3. Same file: add one CRLF control test. Give `extractSnippet` and `extractWrapUpSnippet` a `text` parameter that defaults to the module-level read. For each doc:
   - build a CRLF string from the LF `readText()` result with `.replace(/\n/g, '\r\n')`;
   - assert that the string contains `\r\n` and no `\r\r\n`;
   - write it to a temp file, read it back through `readText()`, and assert the extractor returns the same snippet as for the LF text.

   Remove the temp directory when the test ends. This control pins that the file's read-plus-extract path survives a CRLF checkout on ubuntu-only CI.
4. Sibling follow-up: file one backlog record through `/claude-tweaks:capture` with a spec-shaped body for the ten unclaimed sibling files listed in Current State, so they are not left as an implicit deferral. First re-run the sibling grep and re-check open records, and drop any file that a record claims by then. Record the grep output and the new record number in the PR body.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `node --test tests/pipeline-run-dir-adoption-anchoring.test.js` passes on macOS/Linux with all five existing tests plus the new CRLF control, none skipped or removed.
- [ ] CRLF simulation on macOS/Linux:
  - Build a scratch copy of the repo's `tests/` helpers, this test file and `plugin/`, then convert both skill files to `\r\n`.
  - The pre-fix test fails all five tests with the two extractor messages.
  - The fixed test passes all six.
  - Quote both runs' `# pass` / `# fail` lines in the PR body.
- [ ] The file passes on `windows-latest`. Prove it before merge by dispatching `gh workflow run windows-regression.yml --ref {branch}` and quoting the per-test `ok` lines for this file from the run's log. Do not rely on the run's adjudication verdict alone (see Gotchas). A non-main ref never files an issue. If the dispatch cannot run, say so explicitly. Do not treat an in-process CRLF simulation as a Windows run.
- [ ] The suite still discriminates. Run each doctoring in the same command as its restore, and quote the red lines:
  - Drop the `| grep -E '/[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[^/]*$'` filter from `run-dir-resolution.md`'s snippet: test 5 goes red.
  - Change the anchoring arm `*) RUN_DIR="" ;;` to `*) : ;;`: the shared-snippet trapped-value test goes red.
  - Replace `readText(f)` with a raw `fs.readFileSync(f, 'utf8')` in the new CRLF control: the control goes red.
- [ ] No file under `plugin/` changes. The skill prose and both snippets are correct, and only the test's read and one assertion change.
- [ ] The sibling follow-up record from Deliverable 4 exists, and the PR body names its number along with the re-run grep result.
- [ ] `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Fixed a run-directory test that failed on Windows checkouts because of line-ending and path-format differences.

## Technical Approach

The change is test-side only and follows the "Build CRLF inputs from the LF text" pattern in `.claude/skills/windows-checkout-test-parity/SKILL.md`, plus its two-layer Anti-Patterns row from #3517. `readText()` (`fs.readFileSync(p, 'utf8').replace(/\r\n/g, '\n')`) is the repo's single EOL-normalizing read for governed markdown. `skill-prose-conformance-tests` already requires it for every prose suite.

This suite extracts the snippets and then executes them, so normalizing at the read is the right fix, not a CRLF-tolerant regex. The scratch run showed that a `\r?\n`-only regex fix still hands bash a snippet full of `\r`.

The test-5 assertion changes because the shared snippet's step-2 output is a bash-side path. Under Git Bash it is MSYS-form, so it can never byte-equal a native `path.join` result. The test's claim is which directory gets selected, and the basename carries that claim on every platform. `path.basename` splits on both `/` and `\` on win32, so it handles the MSYS string there too.

Tests 1-4 keep their full-path assertions:

- Test 1 (shared snippet) resolves to `''`, which skips the `startsWith` check.
- Test 2 (shared snippet) passes the native env value through unchanged.
- Tests 3-4 (wrap-up) get native paths back from `resolve-run-dir`.

The `windows-regression.yml` dispatch is the ground truth for whether those predictions hold.

Make Deliverables 1-3 together in one commit. Then run the doctoring checks, then the dispatch. File the Deliverable 4 record during the build, not after merge.

### Key Files

- `tests/pipeline-run-dir-adoption-anchoring.test.js` — the change: the two skill reads (lines 24-31) go through `readText()`; both extractors (lines 33, 47) take a `text` parameter; test 5's assertion (line 147) compares by `path.basename`; a new CRLF control test is added
- `tests/helpers/read-skill.js` — read-only reference: `readText()`
- `plugin/skills/_shared/run-dir-resolution.md` — read-only reference: the `## Bash snippet (resolution)` section (lines 40-67) and its step-2 `find … | grep -E … | sort | tail` line (56)
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/SKILL.md` — read-only reference: `### Establish the run directory (unconditional)` (line 82) and its fenced snippet (lines 88-98)
- `tests/hooks-run-dir-resolve.test.js` — read-only reference: the `path.basename(out.path)` step-2 pins (lines 186, 210) and the native-path equality pins that pass on `windows-latest`
- `.claude/skills/windows-checkout-test-parity/SKILL.md` — read-only reference: the CRLF-input rule and the two-layer snippet-test Anti-Patterns row

## Gotchas

- Do not fix this by making the extraction regexes `\r?\n`-tolerant alone. The captured snippet keeps its `\r`s, and `bash -c` fails with `syntax error near unexpected token $'in\r'`, as the scratch run reproduced. The general advice in `skill-prose-conformance-tests` to "write `\r?\n`" covers extract-and-compare suites. This suite extracts and then executes.
- Do not add a `.gitattributes` `eol=lf` rule for the skill files or `tests/` as the fix. The parity skill scopes `.gitattributes` to the hashed upstream-drift fixtures on purpose.
- Do not "fix" test 5 by translating MSYS paths inside the skill snippet, or by changing `run-dir-resolution.md`. The snippet is the documented reference implementation, and its paths are correct for the shell that runs them. The mismatch exists only in the test's JS-side comparison.
- Test 5's MSYS-path failure is inferred from Git Bash's `pwd` behavior, not observed, because the CRLF failure masks it on Windows today. If the Windows dispatch shows test 5 failing with a different shape, investigate that shape and do not skip the test on win32. One possibility is an empty `resolved` because a non-GNU `find` resolved first on `PATH`.
- A `workflow_dispatch` of `windows-regression.yml` on a branch baselines against the branch's previous commit (`HEAD^1`, see #3568). If the fix is already in that commit, the adjudication verdict proves nothing. Read this file's per-test `ok` / `not ok` lines in the run's log.
- Keep this record to this one test file plus the Deliverable 4 capture. The other unclaimed siblings have the same CRLF shape but different extractors. Some also run what they extract, so a backslash `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` second layer may apply to them, as in #3555 and #3587. Each needs its own Windows proof.

## Original request

Windows regression: 1 test file(s) newly failing after a865bb71d

The post-merge Windows check failed on commit a865bb71d72935471f39c361f48971236d30c56a (compared against 5e116e0ff).

**Merged PR:** #3547 (https://github.com/thn-inc/claude-tweaks/pull/3547)

**Run:** https://github.com/thn-inc/claude-tweaks/actions/runs/39212936982

groups.body:
Surface: infra

**Related:** #3429, #3507, #3509, #3562, #3563, #3565, #3581

## Current State

The post-merge `windows-regression` workflow (run 39213725882, on `windows-latest`) found one test file newly failing after PR #3531 merged as `31d2ce142`. That commit (#3497's change) added `tests/flow-pass-reentry-conformance.test.js`, so this failure is genuinely new rather than inherited. It is still failing on the latest Windows run (39242652806, at `7eaa543fc`), where it now shows as a baseline failure: the base-commit log and the isolated HEAD log both report `# pass 7` / `# fail 1`. Verified against `origin/main` at `1c8cda70b`, where the test file is unchanged since `31d2ce142`.

Exactly one of the file's eight tests fails: `AC2.1 retired limit sentences are gone from every skill file` (line 108). The assertion that fails is the doctored-corpus control at line 127, not the real-corpus check:

```
+   'flow\\x.md: no documented step re-runs the pass'
-   'flow/x.md: no documented step re-runs the pass'
```

Root cause, test-side only. The test's own `walk()` helper (lines 110-118) lists files with `fs.readdirSync(dir, { recursive: true })`. Node joins recursive entries with the native separator, so on win32 the doctored file comes back as `flow\x.md`. The helper then uses that native relative path directly as a display ID (`hits.push(\`${f}: ${phrase}\`)`, line 115), and the control compares the result with the forward-slash literal `'flow/x.md: …'`. The display-ID producer is the test, not plugin code; no file under `plugin/` is involved. The real-corpus assertion `assert.deepEqual(real.hits, [])` passes on Windows only because a clean corpus yields no hits. On a real regression its message would carry the same backslash IDs.

CRLF plays no part. `collapse()` folds `\r` into whitespace, and the file's other section extractors already use `\r?$` and `split(/\r?\n/)`. The other seven tests pass in both Windows logs.

Reproduced in scratch on macOS with a win32 simulation. A `--require` preload makes recursive `fs.readdirSync` return `\`-joined entries, lets `fs.readFileSync` accept `\` the way Windows fs does, and sets `path.sep` to `\`. Run against the `origin/main` copy of the test and `plugin/`:

- Unsimulated, pre-fix: `# pass 8` / `# fail 0`.
- Simulated, pre-fix: `not ok 6 - AC2.1 …`, with the same `+ 'flow\\x.md: …'` / `- 'flow/x.md: …'` diff as the Windows log, and `# pass 7` / `# fail 1`.
- Simulated and unsimulated, with `toPosix` applied at the hit producer: `# pass 8` / `# fail 0`.

The simulation cannot show drive letters, real Windows fs semantics or `path.win32.join` behavior. It reproduces only the separator Node puts into recursive `readdirSync` entries, which is exactly what this failure turns on.

Sibling grep on `origin/main`. `git grep -nE "readdirSync\([^)]*recursive" -- '*.js'` finds this file's line 111 as the only recursive-readdir site in the repo. No `globSync` or async recursive `readdir` call exists. The broader class, a native relative path used as a display ID and compared with `/` keys, also fails on the same latest Windows run in eight other files. All eight are pre-existing baseline failures, not attributable to #3531, and all are out of scope here (see Gotchas).

## Deliverables

1. `tests/flow-pass-reentry-conformance.test.js`: normalize the display ID at its producer. Require `toPosix` from `plugin/bin/lib/shared-primitives.js` and build each hit as `` `${toPosix(String(f), sep)}: ${phrase}` ``, through a small `hitId(f, phrase, sep = path.sep)` helper inside the AC2.1 test. Leave the fs path native: `fs.readFileSync(path.join(dir, String(f)), 'utf8')` keeps the raw `f`.
2. Pin the win32 branch on a Linux-runnable path. In the same test, assert `hitId('flow\\x.md', retired[0], path.win32.sep) === \`flow/x.md: ${retired[0]}\``. A `toPosix` call that takes the default `sep` is otherwise invisible to ubuntu CI: dropping it stays green there (the parity skill's display-ID section). This assertion makes that drop go red on Linux.
3. Leave the doctored-corpus control's expected value as the forward-slash literal `'flow/x.md: no documented step re-runs the pass'`. Do not rebuild it with `path.join`.
4. Before opening the PR, re-run the sibling grep (`git grep -nE "readdirSync\([^)]*recursive|globSync" -- '*.js'`). Fix any new recursive-readdir hit that builds a display ID with the same move. Record the result in the PR body: at shaping time against `origin/main` `1c8cda70b` this file was the only hit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `node --test tests/flow-pass-reentry-conformance.test.js` passes on macOS/Linux with all 8 tests running, none skipped or removed.
- [ ] The same file passes on `windows-latest`. Prove it before merge by dispatching `gh workflow run windows-regression.yml --ref {branch}` and quoting the run's per-file isolated log result for this file (`# pass 8` / `# fail 0`). A non-main ref never files an issue. If the dispatch cannot run, say so explicitly. Do not treat a win32 path simulation as a Windows run.
- [ ] A scratch win32 simulation passes against the fixed test and fails against the pre-fix one with the Windows diff (`'flow\\x.md: …'` vs `'flow/x.md: …'`). The simulation is a `--require` preload that makes recursive `fs.readdirSync` return `\`-joined entries, maps `\` to `/` in `fs.readFileSync`, and sets `path.sep = '\\'`. Quote both runs' `# pass` / `# fail` lines in the PR body.
- [ ] The new `path.win32.sep` pin discriminates on Linux: with `toPosix` removed from `hitId`, an unsimulated `node --test tests/flow-pass-reentry-conformance.test.js` goes red with the `'flow\\x.md: …'` diff. Restore the line in the same command.
- [ ] The retired-phrase check still discriminates: append `no documented step\nre-runs the pass` to a skill file under `plugin/skills/` and the test goes red, naming that file with forward slashes (for example `flow/multi-spec.md: no documented step re-runs the pass`). Restore the file in the same command.
- [ ] No file under `plugin/` changes. The skill prose and `toPosix` are correct; only the test's display-ID construction is wrong.
- [ ] `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Fixed a flow conformance test that failed on Windows because it compared a backslash file path with a forward-slash one.

## Technical Approach

This is a test-side fix that follows the "Display IDs and native paths are two contracts" rule in `.claude/skills/windows-checkout-test-parity/SKILL.md`. A path the code shows or compares as an ID uses `/` on every OS and is normalized at its producer with `shared-primitives.js`'s `toPosix(p, sep = path.sep)`. A path later opened with `fs` stays native. The producer here is the test's own `walk()`, which builds the hit string from a native recursive-readdir entry. So the fix goes there, and the expected literal stays as it is. The skill rejects per-fixture `.replace(/\\/g, '/')` patches and `path.join`-built expectations for display IDs, because they hide a producer that is still wrong.

The `sep` parameter on `hitId` follows the skill's injection pattern: the default stays `path.sep` for the real walk, and the pin passes `path.win32.sep` explicitly. That is the same seam `tests/bin-lib/shared-primitives.test.js` uses for `toPosix` itself. Do not stub `process.platform`.

Verified in scratch: two added lines (the `toPosix` require and the `hitId` helper with its pin) plus the changed `push` turn the simulated run from 7/1 to 8/0, and the unsimulated run stays 8/0.

### Key Files

- `tests/flow-pass-reentry-conformance.test.js` — AC2.1 (lines 108-128): `walk()`'s hit push (line 115) routed through a `toPosix`-based `hitId`, plus a `path.win32.sep` pin; the `fs.readFileSync` path (line 114) and the control's expected literal (line 127) unchanged
- `plugin/bin/lib/shared-primitives.js` — read-only reference: `toPosix(p, sep = path.sep)` (line 208), the shared display-ID normalizer
- `tests/bin-lib/shared-primitives.test.js` — read-only reference: the existing `toPosix` pins under `path.win32.sep` that the new assertion mirrors
- `.claude/skills/windows-checkout-test-parity/SKILL.md` — read-only reference: the display-ID vs native-path rule and the win32-simulation caveats

## Gotchas

- Do not apply `toPosix` to the path passed to `fs.readFileSync`. Native fs paths stay native. Only the reported hit string is a display ID.
- Do not "fix" this by rewriting the expected value to `path.join('flow', 'x.md') + ': …'` or by `.replace(/\\/g, '/')` on the hits array at the assertion. Either one turns the control green while the producer still emits native IDs, and the real-corpus failure message stays backslashed on Windows.
- The win32 simulation is harness evidence, not a Windows run. On POSIX `path.posix === path`, so setting `path.sep` also flips `path.posix.sep`. Run the simulation from a scratch cwd and check `git status` afterwards, since the AC2.1 control writes a temp tree. Only the `gh workflow run windows-regression.yml --ref {branch}` result closes the Windows criterion.
- Keep this record to this one file. The same latest Windows run shows the broader native-display-ID class in eight other files, all pre-existing baseline failures that #3531 did not introduce:

groups.title: Windows regression: 1 test file(s) newly failing after 31d2ce142

groups.body:
Surface: infra

**Related:** #3429, #3507, #3509, #3562, #3563, #3564, #3581, #3587, #3574

## Current State

The post-merge `windows-regression` workflow (run 39214085383, on `windows-latest`) flagged three test files as newly failing after PR #3530 merged #3520 as `9dc2c1df4` (base `31d2ce142`). #3520 added every test that fails here. All three files still fail on the latest run, 39242652806 at `7eaa543fc` (base `df15212d5`), where they are now adjudicated as baseline failures. A baseline failure is never re-flagged, so only this fix will clear them. Verified against `origin/main` at `1c8cda70b`: none of the three test files, `tests/helpers/read-skill.js`, or `plugin/skills/dispatch/` has changed since `7eaa543fc`.

Per-file breakdown from the latest run's isolated logs. There are five failing tests and three root causes, all test-side.

1. **`tests/console-autoresolve-drain-overlap-carveout.test.js`: 4/6 pass. Two tests fail on a CRLF read.** The failing tests are `near-duplicate Step 6 hold template is parsed by drainOverlapHoldPrs (AC7)` (line 88) and its `go-red control: …` (line 93). Both fail inside `nearDuplicateHoldTemplate` (lines 70-76) with `drain-pr-overlap.md has a fenced Auto-merge gate template with the near-duplicate suffix`. That helper reads `plugin/skills/dispatch/drain-pr-overlap.md` with a raw `fs.readFileSync` (line 71) and extracts fences with `/```\n([\s\S]*?)\n```/g` (line 72). On a `core.autocrlf=true` checkout every fence line ends in `\r\n`, so the regex matches no fence. The other four tests read through `collapse()`, which turns `\r\n` into a space, so they are unaffected.
2. **`tests/dispatch-near-dup-pairs-script.test.js`: 1/3 pass. Two tests fail on a CRLF read, and a second failure is hidden behind it.** `AC8.1: the heredoc warns on every cross-group pair …` (line 64) and `Review Focus 4: a pull with no strong pair rewrites a stale pairs file to []` (line 85) both fail in `heredoc()` with `the #1944 heredoc has no NODE_EVAL_EOF terminator`. `QUEUE_PULL` is a raw read (line 16), and the terminator search is `'\n' + 'NODE_EVAL_EOF\n'` (lines 20 and 28), which never matches `\r\nNODE_EVAL_EOF\r\n`. Behind that, `run()` (line 56) passes the native `path.join(ROOT, 'plugin')` as `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`. The #1944 heredoc in `plugin/skills/dispatch/queue-pull-script.md` (lines 685-690) is unquoted, so bash expands that value into `require('${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/lib/dispatch/near-dup-pairs.js')`. A `D:\a\…` value then becomes JS escapes, the same `Cannot find module 'D:aclaude-tweaks…'` failure #3517 hit after its CRLF fix.
3. **`tests/dispatch-per-record-groups-prose.test.js`: 13/14 pass. One test fails because Windows has no `/bin/sh`.** The record's excerpt quotes `AC2.1: the neighbour-in-flight heredoc runs offline …` with `Cannot find module 'D:aclaude-tweaks…'`. That test was already failing at base `31d2ce142`. #3518 has since fixed it (`e4d6b12bf`, forward-slash `PLUGIN_DIR`), and it passes on the latest run. The test #3520 added, and the one that still fails, is `a failed neighbour-in-flight pool fetch writes an empty pool and says so, so nothing is excluded (#3278)` (line 185), with `null !== 0` and no stderr. It runs `spawnSync('/bin/sh', ['-c', poolFetchBlock()], { env: { PATH: dir, … } })` (line 190). On win32 `/bin/sh` resolves to `D:\bin\sh`, which does not exist, so the spawn fails with `ENOENT`, `status` is `null`, and `stderr` is empty. A bare `'sh'` would not fix it, because Node looks the command up through the child env's `PATH`, which the test deliberately points at an empty dir so `gh` is unreachable.

**Reproduction (macOS, a simulation and not a Windows run).** `git archive origin/main` of `tests/` and `plugin/` was extracted into scratch, and every `plugin/**/*.md` and `docs/**/*.md` was converted to CRLF.

- Before the fix, the LF tree passed 23/23. The CRLF tree failed exactly the four CRLF tests above with the Windows error strings.
- Feeding the #1944 heredoc through `bash` with `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT=D:\a\claude-tweaks\claude-tweaks\plugin` turned the `require` specifier into `D:aclaude-tweaksclaude-tweaksplugin/bin/lib/dispatch/near-dup-pairs.js`. The forward-slash root kept it intact.
- `spawnSync` of a missing absolute shell, and of bare `'sh'` under `env: { PATH: emptyDir }`, both returned `status=null error=ENOENT` with no stderr, the Windows failure's exact shape.
- After the fix described below, the CRLF tree and the LF tree each passed 25/25.

The `/bin/sh` failure itself can only be shown on a real Windows runner.

**Sibling sweep** of `tests/` on `origin/main` `1c8cda70b` for the three shapes:

- **In scope:** `tests/dispatch-named-target-exclusion-fixture.test.js`. It has the same two-layer defect against the same skill file: a raw `queue-pull-script.md` read (line 32), a `<<NODE_EVAL_EOF\n` start anchor (line 45), and a native `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` passed to `bash -c` (line 99). It fails at the latest run's baseline with `extraction start anchor not found in queue-pull-script.md`, which reproduced exactly under CRLF in scratch and passed after the same fix. No open record owns it.
- **Out of scope, owned elsewhere:** `spawnSync('/bin/sh', …)` in `tests/bin-lib/harness-health/cli-validate-findings.test.js:442,467` (masked behind #3563's failures) and `execFileSync('/bin/sh', …)` in `tests/verify-expectations-writer-conformance.test.js:66` (masked behind #3562's CRLF extraction failure).
- **Out of scope, already handled:** `tests/build-ac-forwarding-verification.test.js:60` already skips on win32 for its `/bin/sh` use.
- **False positive:** `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/release-merged.test.js`'s `EOF\n` hits are in-test stub literals, not a skill read.

## Deliverables

1. `tests/console-autoresolve-drain-overlap-carveout.test.js`: read `drain-pr-overlap.md` once through `tests/helpers/read-skill.js`'s `readText()`. Give `nearDuplicateHoldTemplate` an optional text parameter that defaults to that read and LF-normalizes its input before the fence regex. Add a CRLF case: `nearDuplicateHoldTemplate(text.replace(/\n/g, '\r\n'))` returns the same template as the LF read, and the built input contains `\r\n` and no `\r\r\n`. Leave the `collapse()`-based reads (line 23) unchanged.
2. `tests/dispatch-near-dup-pairs-script.test.js`:
   - Read `queue-pull-script.md` through `readText()`.
   - Give `heredoc()` an optional source parameter that LF-normalizes, and add the same CRLF-vs-LF extractor case.
   - Pass `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` with forward slashes from one module-level constant (`path.join(ROOT, 'plugin').split(path.sep).join('/')`), with a one-line comment naming the JS-string-literal reason, as `tests/dispatch-neighbour-in-flight-mcp.test.js:72-74` does.
3. `tests/dispatch-per-record-groups-prose.test.js`, the pool-fetch test (line 185): stop depending on `/bin/sh`.
   - Preferred: run the block with `bash`, looked up through the inherited environment (`env: { ...process.env, EMPTY_PATH: dir, DISPATCH_IN_FLIGHT_RAW: rawPath }`). Make `gh` unreachable inside the script by prefixing it with `PATH="$EMPTY_PATH"`, not through the spawn env's `PATH`. The sibling `bash -c` suites already pass on `windows-latest` with that spawn shape.
   - Before the status assertion, assert `result.error` is `undefined`, so a spawn failure names itself instead of reading `null !== 0`.
   - If the dispatched Windows run shows the in-script `PATH` does not hide `gh` there, fall back to `tests/build-ac-forwarding-verification.test.js:60`'s `{ skip: process.platform === 'win32' && '<reason>' }` form for this one test, and say so in the PR body.
4. `tests/dispatch-named-target-exclusion-fixture.test.js` (sweep hit): read `queue-pull-script.md` through `readText()` (line 32), and pass a forward-slash `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` (line 99).
5. Before opening the PR, re-run the sweep over `tests/`:
   - a raw read of a tracked markdown file searched with a `\n`-anchored fence or `NODE_EVAL_EOF` anchor;
   - `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT: path.join(` without `.split(path.sep)`;
   - `'/bin/sh'` / `'/bin/bash'` as a spawn target.

   Fix any new unowned hit with the same move, and record the result and the owner of each remaining hit in the PR body.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `node --test tests/console-autoresolve-drain-overlap-carveout.test.js tests/dispatch-near-dup-pairs-script.test.js tests/dispatch-per-record-groups-prose.test.js tests/dispatch-named-target-exclusion-fixture.test.js` passes on macOS/Linux with no test removed or weakened.
- [ ] All four files pass on `windows-latest`. Prove it before merge by dispatching `gh workflow run windows-regression.yml --ref {branch}`. Quote that run's per-file isolated result for each of the four files: the pool-fetch test must report `ok`, not `# SKIP`, unless Deliverable 3's fallback was taken and the PR body says so. A non-main ref never files an issue. If the dispatch cannot run, say so explicitly. A CRLF or `path.win32` simulation on macOS/Linux is not a Windows run.
- [ ] On macOS/Linux, a CRLF-checkout simulation passes: a scratch copy of the tree with `plugin/**/*.md` converted to `\r\n` runs the four files green. Against the pre-fix tests, the same simulation fails the two drain-overlap tests, the two near-dup-pairs tests and the named-target test with their Windows error strings.
- [ ] The new CRLF cases discriminate. Temporarily remove the LF normalization inside `nearDuplicateHoldTemplate` and inside `heredoc()`, and each CRLF case goes red (`… fenced Auto-merge gate template …` / `… no NODE_EVAL_EOF terminator`). Restore both files in the same command.
- [ ] The pool-fetch test discriminates. Temporarily put an executable `gh` stub that prints `[]` and exits 0 into the test's empty dir (POSIX only), and the test goes red on the missing `AUTO — dispatch: neighbour-in-flight pool fetch failed …` line. Restore the file in the same command.
- [ ] No file under `plugin/` changes. The skill prose, the heredocs and `plugin/bin/lib/` are correct; only the tests' reads, substitutions and shell choice are platform-dependent.
- [ ] `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Fixed six dispatch and console prose tests that failed only on Windows checkouts.

## Technical Approach

The fix is test-side only, following `.claude/skills/windows-checkout-test-parity/SKILL.md`. Three of its rules apply:

- "A test extracts regions from live skill markdown → a CRLF input proving the extractor still finds the region" covers causes 1 and 2. `readText()` is the repo's single normalizing read. Normalizing again inside the extractor is what lets the CRLF case go red on Linux CI, as #3518 did with `refusalFenceBody`.
- The Anti-Patterns row "Treating a CRLF fix as the whole Windows fix for a test that extracts and runs a skill's shell snippet" covers the masked backslash-root layer in cause 2 and in the named-target sibling. #3517 and #3518 already fixed the identical shape this way (`tests/dispatch-neighbour-in-flight-mcp.test.js:74`, `tests/dispatch-per-record-groups-prose.test.js`'s `PLUGIN_DIR`).
- "Keep a win32-only real-process round-trip as the ground truth" is why cause 3 prefers running the block through a real shell on Windows over skipping it.

The pool-fetch test's `PATH` moves from the spawn env into the script because the spawn env's `PATH` is also what Node uses to find the shell. Overriding it there forces an absolute shell path, and Windows has no portable one. Assigning `PATH` inside the script leaves the shell lookup on the inherited environment and still hides `gh` from the block. All of the block's remaining commands (`echo`, redirections) are shell builtins.

The product-side question of whether a real Windows Claude Code install hands Git Bash a backslash `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` belongs to #3555. This record does not touch the heredocs.

### Key Files

- `tests/console-autoresolve-drain-overlap-carveout.test.js` — `readText()` read of `drain-pr-overlap.md`; `nearDuplicateHoldTemplate` (lines 70-76) takes text and LF-normalizes; new CRLF extractor case
- `tests/dispatch-near-dup-pairs-script.test.js` — `readText()` read (line 16); `heredoc()` (lines 23-31) takes a source and LF-normalizes; forward-slash `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` in `run()` (line 56); new CRLF extractor case
- `tests/dispatch-per-record-groups-prose.test.js` — pool-fetch test (lines 185-197): `bash` with an in-script `PATH="$EMPTY_PATH"` and a `result.error` assertion, replacing `spawnSync('/bin/sh', …)`
- `tests/dispatch-named-target-exclusion-fixture.test.js` — `readText()` read (line 32) and forward-slash `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` (line 99)
- `tests/helpers/read-skill.js` — read-only reference: the shared `readText()` EOL-normalizing read
- `tests/dispatch-neighbour-in-flight-mcp.test.js` — read-only reference: the #3517 precedent (forward-slash `PLUGIN_ROOT`, line 74; CRLF-vs-LF snippet case)
- `tests/build-ac-forwarding-verification.test.js` — read-only reference: the win32 `/bin/sh` skip form (line 60), Deliverable 3's fallback only
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/drain-pr-overlap.md` — read-only reference: the near-duplicate Auto-merge gate fence (lines 97-99)
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/queue-pull-script.md` — read-only reference: the pool-fetch block (lines 615-618), the named-target heredoc, and the #1944 heredoc (lines 685-690)

## Gotchas

- Do not fix the CRLF failures with a `.gitattributes` `eol=lf` rule, and do not loosen the extractors to accept `\r\r\n` or bare `\r`. The parity skill keeps `.gitattributes` scoped to the hashed upstream fixtures on purpose.
- Do not build a CRLF case from a raw read (`raw.replace(/\n/g, '\r\n')`). On a Windows checkout that yields `\r\r\n` (#3523). Build it from the `readText()` value and assert there is no `\r\r\n`.
- The pool-fetch test passes for the wrong reason if `gh` is reachable but fails for an unrelated cause, such as no auth or no git repo in cwd. That is why its go-red control plants a succeeding `gh` stub instead of relying on the real CLI. Keep the in-script `PATH` line as the block's first line, so nothing in the block runs before it.
- If the Windows run fails the pool-fetch test only on the `AUTO — dispatch: …` stderr match while the empty-pool assertion passes, suspect em-dash encoding through Git Bash's `echo`. Set a UTF-8 locale in the spawned env (`LC_ALL: 'C.UTF-8'`) rather than loosening the regex.
- Fixing only the excerpted test misses its siblings. The `per-record` excerpt names a test that #3518 already fixed; the failing one is the pool-fetch test. Read each file's isolated log from the dispatched run, not the record's excerpt, before calling the fix done.
- Keep the scope to these four files. `cli-validate-findings` (#3563) and `verify-expectations-writer-conformance` (#3562) also spawn `/bin/sh`, but their own records own them. Other open `Windows regression:` records (#3429, #3507, #3509, #3562, #3563, #3564, #3581) cover other commits and files.

## Original request

The post-merge Windows check failed on commit 9dc2c1df496df79bf9b22e3a21345458617efe62 (compared against 31d2ce142).

groups.title: Windows regression: 3 test file(s) newly failing after 9dc2c1df4

groups.body:
Surface: infra

**Related:** #3429, #3507, #3509, #3562, #3563, #3564, #3565, #3543

## Current State

The post-merge `windows-regression` workflow (run 39229351955, on `windows-latest`) flagged two test files after PR #3533 merged #3416 as `dcdd58863`: `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/archive-merged.test.js` and `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/release-merged.test.js`. The production code is not at fault in either file. Every failure comes from the way the tests fake `gh`.

**The excerpts are misleading.** Both quoted tests also fail at the base commit `3bf097c8e`. The run's `verify-report` artifact shows `archive-merged.test.js:1928` ("a main-loop decideArchive skip (no-pr)…") among 19 failures at base, and `release-merged.test.js:246` ("Phase 1.5 resolves prState via the pool…") among 17 failures at base. The filer quotes the first failure in each file. It flagged the files because #3416 added new tests that fail for the same reason:

| File | Base `3bf097c8e` | HEAD `dcdd58863` | Newly failing (all added by #3416) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `archive-merged.test.js` | 19 of 119 fail | 26 of 128 fail | AC5.1, AC5.2, AC5.1 fail-closed, AC1.1, AC1.1 orthogonal, AC2.1, AC4.1 (current lines 2738, 2747, 2755, 2831, 2852, 2889, 2909) |
| `release-merged.test.js` | 17 of 50 fail | 18 of 53 fail | "resolves by stamped pr.number ahead of the live-worktree branch join" and "AC3.1 AC3.2: a live claim whose stamped pr.number is OPEN…" |

**`release-merged.test.js` is already fixed, and this record has no work in it.** `1ed26d947` (#3506, merged after `dcdd58863`) added the per-file `PATH_STUB_SKIP` constant to all 19 stub-installing tests in that file, including the #3416 ones. On the latest `windows-latest` run (39242652806, `7eaa543fc`, which contains `1ed26d947`), the file is not in `baselineAdjudicated.failingFiles`. That run's `verify-logs/tests.log` reports `releaseMerged: Phase 1.5 resolves prState…` as `ok … # SKIP win32: execFileSync("gh") never spawns a \#!/bin/sh stub named gh on PATH`, and it reports 41 such skip lines in total: 22 from `pr-state.test.js` and 19 from `release-merged.test.js`. It was not flaky. Its 1835 ms duration is the real `gh.exe` network round-trip described below. A scripted pass over the file at `origin/main` `1c8cda70b` shows that the set of tests that install a stub equals the set that carries `PATH_STUB_SKIP`, exactly.

**`archive-merged.test.js` still fails.** On the latest run it fails 26 of 128 tests at both HEAD and base, so the filer no longer counts it as new. It stays in the Windows baseline set until it is fixed. The file has not changed since `dcdd58863`.

**Root cause, test-side only.** `archive-merged.js` resolves PR and issue state through `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/pr-state.js`, which calls `execFileSync('gh', …)` and `execFile('gh', …)`. Both are bound when the module is required and have no injection point. The test file fakes `gh` by writing a `#!/bin/sh` script named `gh` (no extension) into a temp directory and putting that directory first on `PATH`. Three helpers do this: `installGhWrapper` (line 91), `installGhPrWrapper` (line 124) and `installGhIssueStateWrapper` (line 156). On win32, Node's (libuv's) command lookup appends `.com` and `.exe` to an extensionless name and never runs an extensionless file, so the stub is invisible. The runner's own `gh.exe` answers instead. The job has `GH_TOKEN` set, so that real `gh` makes an authenticated call for a fixture repository that does not exist (`acme/w`, or no remote at all), exits non-zero, and `classifyExecError` correctly reports `network-failure`. That is the excerpt's `"reason":"network-failure"`. The product classification is right: a real `gh.exe` ran and failed. This is not a Windows launch failure misread as an answer, because `gh` ships as `gh.exe` on Windows and lookup finds it. This is the same defect #3506 fixed in the two sibling files.

**The fix is reproduced by simulation, not by a Windows run.** A scratch `--require` preload swapped `child_process`'s `execFileSync`/`execFile`/`spawn`/`spawnSync` so that a bare `gh` resolves the way win32 resolves it: try `gh.com`/`gh.exe` on `PATH`, otherwise use a fake runner `gh` that prints `no git remotes found` and exits 1. It changed nothing else. Results against the `origin/main` files:

- `archive-merged.test.js` without the preload: `# tests 128`, `# pass 128`, `# fail 0`.
- With the preload: `# pass 102`, `# fail 26`. The failing set is identical, by test name, to the 26 in the latest Windows run's isolated log (`diff` empty). The failure-reason tallies are identical too (7× `+ 'network-failure'`, 4× `+ 'no-branch'`, 5× `- 'console-never-rendered'`, 3× `- 'pr-open'`, …). The line-1928 test fails with the excerpt's exact message (`expected a no-pr skip, got {… "reason":"network-failure"}`). The fake runner logged the call it received: `pr list --head feat-nopr-main-1733 --state all --json …`.
- As a control, the same preload on `release-merged.test.js` reproduces exactly the 18 failures of the original run's HEAD log.
- With a scratch copy of the fix (the `PATH_STUB_SKIP` constant on the 31 stub-installing tests, forced on by an env var because the simulation cannot make `process.platform` report `win32`): `# pass 97`, `# fail 0`, `# skipped 31` under the preload, and `# pass 128`, `# skipped 0` on POSIX without it.

What the simulation cannot show: real `cmd.exe`/libuv behavior, drive letters, or any other win32-only failure hiding behind these. Only a `windows-latest` run proves the file green.

**Which tests install a stub.** A scripted pass over every top-level `test(`, following calls into helpers (`fixtureOrdinaryMergedNoConsole` calls `installGhWrapper`), finds 31 of 128 that install a stub:

- **The 26 that fail on Windows.** Lines 1928, 1965, 2194, 2212, 2249, 2270, 2314, 2339, 2396, 2425, 2464, 2499, 2549, 2590, 2669, 2678, 2685, 2701, 2738, 2747, 2755, 2831, 2852, 2889, 2909 and 3338.
- **5 that pass on Windows, but only vacuously.**
  - Lines 1752 and 1858 install the stub only as a "belt-and-braces guard" (their own comment). Their assertions read an injected runner and cache I/O, and on win32 the guard cannot work.
  - Lines 2365, 2869 and 3356 expect an outcome (fall back to `no-branch`, skip `network-failure`, stay in place) that a failing real `gh` produces just as well as the stub does.

The other 97 tests install no stub and pass on Windows today.

**Sibling grep (`origin/main` `1c8cda70b`).** Grepping `tests/` for files that write a `#!/bin/sh` `gh` or `git` shim and touch `PATH` finds 10 files:

They need a different fix and stay in the #2767 baseline set |

Every out-of-scope file was already failing at base on the latest run (`baselineFailing`), so each sits in the open Windows-baseline record #2767.

## Deliverables

1. In `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/archive-merged.test.js`, add the same per-file constant the two sibling files use, with the identical reason string: `const PATH_STUB_SKIP = process.platform === 'win32' && 'win32: execFileSync("gh") never spawns a #!/bin/sh stub named gh on PATH';`. Put it after the `require` block.
2. Add `{ skip: PATH_STUB_SKIP }` as the options argument of every `test(` whose body, or a helper it calls, installs a `gh` stub on `PATH` through `installGhWrapper`, `installGhPrWrapper` or `installGhIssueStateWrapper`. That was 31 tests at shaping time (the lines listed in Current State). Re-derive the set from the file at build time, because #3503 or another merge may add stub tests first. Include the 5 vacuous passers: the rule is "writes a stub", not "fails today". Leave every test that installs no stub unchanged, so it keeps running on Windows.
3. Change no production code and no helper body. In the PR body, state the final stub-test count and the scripted check that produced it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every top-level `test(` in `archive-merged.test.js` whose body, or a helper it calls, invokes `installGhWrapper`, `installGhPrWrapper` or `installGhIssueStateWrapper` carries `{ skip: PATH_STUB_SKIP }`, and no other `test(` does. Prove it with a scripted pass and quote its output: the stub-installing set equals the `PATH_STUB_SKIP` set.
- [ ] `PATH_STUB_SKIP`'s reason string is byte-identical to the constants in `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/pr-state.test.js` and `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/release-merged.test.js`.
- [ ] On POSIX, `node --test tests/bin-lib/reconcile/archive-merged.test.js` passes with zero skipped tests. Quote the raw `ℹ tests` / `ℹ pass` / `ℹ fail` / `ℹ skipped` lines.
- [ ] The stub tests still discriminate on POSIX. With the fix applied, temporarily change the line-1928 test's `installGhWrapper([])` to return one OPEN PR for its branch, and that test goes red (it no longer gets a `no-pr` skip). Restore the file in the same command.
- [ ] The file passes on `windows-latest`. Prove it before merge by dispatching `gh workflow run windows-regression.yml --ref {branch}` and quoting the run's result for this file. In the run's `verify-report.json`, `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/archive-merged.test.js` is absent from `baselineAdjudicated.failingFiles`. In its `verify-logs/tests.log`, the stub tests show `# SKIP win32: execFileSync("gh") never spawns…`, and the file's other tests are reported `ok` with no SKIP. A non-main ref never files an issue. If the dispatch cannot run, say so explicitly. Do not treat the gh-lookup simulation as a Windows run.
- [ ] No file under `plugin/` changes.
- [ ] `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Fixed a reconciler test suite that failed on Windows checkouts because its fake GitHub CLI never ran there, with no change to plugin behavior.

## Technical Approach

This is a test-side fix that applies #3506's ruling to the third file with the same defect. Behavior only one platform can produce gets a per-test `skip` with a stated reason. `tests/console-execute.test.js` (#3358) and the two sibling reconcile suites already do this.

Rejected: giving `pr-state.js` an injectable runner, so the tests stop faking `gh` through `PATH`. #3506 rejected it because that would change a production module that `archive-merged.js`, `release-merged.js`, `reap-merged.js` and others depend on, for a test-only platform gap. The resolver logic is platform-neutral, and the POSIX run covers it.

Also rejected: a `gh.cmd` stub next to the extensionless one. libuv appends only `.com`/`.exe` for a bare name, so it would never be found either. A `.cmd` would also need the `cmd.exe` launch path the parity skill warns about.

Keep the skip per test, not file-wide: 97 tests install no stub and pass on Windows today.

To re-derive the stub set, a small Node script splits the file at top-level `test(` / `function` boundaries. It marks a test when its body, or any helper it calls (transitively), calls an `installGh*` helper. At shaping time that took one indirection: `fixtureOrdinaryMergedNoConsole` calls `installGhWrapper`.

For local evidence before the Windows dispatch, use the shaping-time simulation from Current State. It is a scratch `--require` preload that resolves a bare `gh` the way win32 does: `.com`/`.exe` only, otherwise a fake runner `gh` that exits 1. Run it from a scratch cwd, never from the worktree. It must give `wrapped[util.promisify.custom]` a promise form, because `pr-state.js` calls `promisify(execFile)` when it loads. Report its result as a simulation.

### Key Files

- `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/archive-merged.test.js` — add `PATH_STUB_SKIP` after the requires, and `{ skip: PATH_STUB_SKIP }` on the 31 stub-installing tests (helpers at lines 91, 124, 156)
- `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/release-merged.test.js` — read-only reference: the `PATH_STUB_SKIP` constant and per-test placement to mirror (#3506)
- `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/pr-state.test.js` — read-only reference: the same constant and reason string
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/pr-state.js` — read-only reference: the `execFileSync('gh')` / `promisify(execFile)` call sites and `classifyExecError`, which correctly maps a real `gh.exe` failure to `network-failure`. No change
- `.github/workflows/windows-regression.yml` — read-only reference: `GH_TOKEN` on the `windows` job, which is why the unstubbed real `gh` makes a network call; also the dispatch target for the proof AC

## Gotchas

- Do not read the excerpt as the regression. The line-1928 test failed at base too. #3416's own seven tests are what made the file newly failing. Diff the per-test `not ok` sets in the run's `verify-logs/`, not the excerpt.
- Do not touch `release-merged.test.js`. It was fixed by `1ed26d947` before this record was shaped, and the latest Windows run shows all 19 of its stub tests skipped.
- Do not "fix" this by remapping `network-failure` in `pr-state.js` or `archive-merged.js`. A real `gh.exe` ran and failed, and `network-failure` is the correct answer to that.
- `reap-merged.test.js` uses the same `installGhWrapper` idiom, but its `#2566` tests exist to exercise win32 behavior. Skipping them on win32 would remove the only platform they test. Keep it, and the `git`-shim files, out of this record; they stay in #2767's baseline set. Do not widen this into a shared `tests/helpers/` stub helper without a separate record (#3506's ruling).
- The ready record #3503 is likely to add `archive-merged` tests. Any new stub-installing test must carry `PATH_STUB_SKIP`. Whichever PR lands second rebases and re-runs the scripted set check.
- Do not edit `.claude/skills/windows-checkout-test-parity/SKILL.md` here. #3579 owns the PATH-stub anti-pattern row.
- Never stub `process.platform` in a committed test to exercise the skip. It is process-global (`windows-checkout-test-parity` Anti-Patterns). The scratch simulation forces the skip through an env var in a throwaway copy only.
